sources.argumentOfPeriapsis: Inglis et al. (2026, AJ 171, 280; doi:10.3847/1538-3881/ae4b34), Table 2: the orbitize! MCMC fit to Keck NIRC speckle, SPHERE and NIRC2 relative astrometry of B around A, 2001-2022; posterior medians. omega = 58 +2/-3 degrees. Astrometry alone cannot tell (omega, Omega) from (omega + 180, Omega + 180), and the paper reports both node solutions, 150 and 330 degrees (section 4, mutual inclination). Its medians take omega and Omega from opposite solutions: with them as printed, orbitize! puts B 180 degrees from every Table 1 position at the right separation. The solution with the printed Omega = 150 has the companion's omega = 238 degrees, stored as A's, 58; packages/astronomy/src/hostedOrbits.test.ts reproduces all seven Table 1 positions with it.
sources.phase: Inglis et al. (2026, AJ 171, 280; doi:10.3847/1538-3881/ae4b34), Table 2: the orbitize! MCMC fit to Keck NIRC speckle, SPHERE and NIRC2 relative astrometry of B around A, 2001-2022; posterior medians. tau = 0.32 +/- 0.03 of a period after t_ref = MJD 55197 (2010.0): MJD 55197 + 0.32 x 31 x 365.25 = 58820.3, taken as BMJD_TDB. The table's derived t_p, 'MJD 55207 +/- 0.08', does not follow from its own tau and period and is not used.
